title: Adaptive Traffic Path Wizard — lightweight dual-path rollout experience
creator: Marina Khatri
description:
Problem: Customers (platform teams + product owners) need a fast, low-friction way to create staged rollouts that balance safety and speed. Existing visual composers are powerful but heavy for common cases (quick canary or A/B) and require multiple screens or presets. This ticket designs a lightweight 'Adaptive Traffic Path Wizard' — a two-path flow (Quick Canary vs Experimented Split) that reduces cognitive overhead for power and non-power users while preserving advanced options behind an explicit 'Advanced' drawer.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-create a safe rollout by 50% for common patterns (canary ramp, even A/B split).
- Surface essential metrics and rollback controls inline, minimizing context switches to dashboards.
- Make rollback paths explicit and discoverable (auto-suggested rollback button + runbook link).
- Provide a simulation preview that shows expected traffic proportions and latency/cost delta estimates before activation.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Must integrate with existing rollout backend policies (route variants, percent-based splits, duration windows).
- Metric snapshots shown are limited to 30m windows for performance and to avoid query cost.
- Advanced targeting (cohorts, feature flags) stays behind the advanced drawer to keep the wizard compact.

Audience: PMs, release engineers, SREs, and product engineers launching model changes or config experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard presents two primary paths (Quick Canary, Experiment Split) with single-screen creation for Quick Canary
Inline metric previews show baseline vs candidate for latency and error rate (30m snapshot) and a cost delta estimate
Rollback action and canary abort options are visible prior to activation and in the rollout detail screen
Simulation preview updates in near-real time when changing traffic percentages and duration
Design spec with annotated components, states, and accessibility notes is uploaded to the design library
Handoff-ready Figma file and prototype link provided; dev acceptance confirms integration hooks (API payload shape)

decisions: Adopt two-path UX: Quick Canary (single screen) + Experiment Split (guided multi-step but still compact)
Show three focus metrics inline: latency (p50/p95), error rate, and cost delta. Other metrics available via 'More metrics' expansion.
Rollback affordance: persistent 'Abort Canary' button + pre-populated rollback runbook link; abort action writes an audit event and surfaces suggested rollback percentage steps.
Simulation will use approximate cost-per-token model (rounded) to avoid expensive queries; exact cost breakdown remains in the cost dashboard link.

notes: This design aims to replace ad-hoc rollout creation flows used in internal beta and be the default quick path in the new rollout composer. Avoids heavy visual canvases for low-risk canaries while keeping advanced controls discoverable. Prototype includes keyboard-first accessibility states and tests color contrast for status chips.
